method: Capture every successful Rust GlobalAlloc alloc/alloc_zeroed/realloc request inside the checked continuous post-JSON input-admission/native-execution/output-materialization window into a fixed bounded array. System backtrace supplies raw return PCs. No event/reentrant loss or stack truncation. Map only own-executable text with verified Mach-O symbols and ASLR slide.
limitations: Counts cover continuous post-JSON requests and requested bytes, not CPU time or live/peak memory.
GlobalAlloc hooks cover Rust requests, matching existing resource counters; direct C allocator calls are outside both measurements.
Inclusive stack counts overlap and must not be added. Inlining may attribute an allocation to a containing function.
Backtrace overhead and the fixed diagnostic buffer change timings and memory; these runs are excluded from latency/resource comparisons.

header.window: One continuous post-JSON interval through native input admission, setup, output allocation, invocation/internal cleanup and RelatedPosts materialization; excludes restoration, JSON IO and post-interval destruction.
